description: conj:im-q-physical-role candidate (i) assigns chirality to arg q. The corpus assigns it to the bar involution q -> 1/q (three citations), and the two operations coincide EXACTLY on |q| = 1 and nowhere else. The substrate has |q_0| = 1.10998, so at the substrate the corpus's chirality flip is 1/q_0 = 0.9009182840 -- a REAL number needing no Im q. Second leg: granting candidate (i)'s identification anyway, Schwarz reflection plus a parity-even Q_beta forces Im q = 0 via the merged im_qbeta_zero_iff theorems.
q0AnchorReason: AGENTS.md 2026-08-07 owner directive: proton is the default for all new compute; this is neither a proton-vs-muon comparison nor an ideal-CAL statement

data.candidate_i_identification: chirality flip = q -> conj(q); arg q is the chirality coordinate
data.corpus_identification: chirality flip = q -> 1/q (bar involution, mirror knot)

data.candidate_i_regime: 'near the unit circle', Kashaev q = exp(2 pi i / N) -- where the identification IS correct
data.physics_premise_for_leg_two: 'Q_beta is chirality-invariant' -- a Q-value is a parity-even energy. This is PHYSICS, not a corpus theorem, and is carried as an explicit Lean hypothesis, never assumed inside a proof. Leg one needs no such premise.
data.scope: (b) for leg one -- an exact algebraic identity (conj = inv iff |q|=1) plus three corpus citations, no numerical near-miss. Leg two is conditional on the stated premise. BOTH are scoped to the ARCHIMEDEAN evaluation at the substrate.
data.does_not_close: the FIBRE level, where AGENTS.md's fibre-vs-observable banner leaves Im q unconstrained and where the Kashaev root-of-unity regime actually lives. Candidate (i) may be right on the fibre; what closes is its archimedean reading.
data.positive_content: the chirality the conjecture went looking for in Im q is already in the corpus at real q, as the bar involution's P_skew content (rem:im-q-vs-p-skew) -- which that same block says is 'kept then discarded' by the canonical P_avg projection.
